questions.prompt: The one-way ANOVA hypotheses for 4 server configs are:
options: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃ = μ₄ vs H₁: at least one mean differs
H₀: all means differ vs H₁: all equal
H₀: σ₁ = σ₂ = σ₃ = σ₄ vs H₁: variances differ
questions.explain: H₁ is **'at least one differs'** — never 'all differ'. (And it's about MEANS; equal variances is an assumption, not the hypothesis.)

questions.prompt: k = 4 groups, n = 6 per group. df₂ (within) = ?
Between-group estimate n·s_x̄² = 2810.153, within-group s_p² = 53.275. F₀ = ? (1 decimal)
questions.explain: F₀ = 2810.153/53.275 = **52.748** ≫ F(0.05; 3, 20) = 3.098 → reject: the server configurations differ significantly in mean response time (the drill's 20-marker).

questions.prompt: You compute F₀ = 0.74. Without any table you already know:
options: Fail to reject H₀ — critical F values are always > 1; between-variation is smaller than within-noise
questions.explain: **F₀ < 1 ⇒ automatic fail-to-reject** for any reasonable α/df: the groups differ LESS than their internal noise predicts. (Drill P3's SSD brands: F = 0.743.)

questions.prompt: Group means 82.6, 71.8, 88.2 (n = 5 each), variance of the means s_x̄² = 69.493. Between-group estimate = n·s_x̄² = ? (1 decimal)
A significant ANOVA (reject H₀) tells you:
options: At least one mean differs — but NOT which one (that needs post-hoc comparisons)
All groups differ from each other
questions.explain: ANOVA's conclusion stops at 'not all equal'. Pointing at the winner needs **post-hoc tests** (outside this syllabus) — quoting this limitation is a free theory mark.

options: Hypotheses → group means + variances → between estimate (n·s_x̄²) → within estimate (mean of s²) → F₀ → df pair + critical F → compare + conclusion sentence
Just compute F and circle it
questions.explain: Q6's 20 marks are spread across the steps: hypotheses (2), group stats (6), between (3), within (2), F (2), df + critical (2), decision + sentence (3). Show EVERY step — partial credit is the safety net.
